key_insight: LingBot-Video adapts large-scale video pretraining for embodied intelligence by using a Mixture-of-Experts DiT design, aiming to improve both efficiency and physical relevance. The core idea is to move video models away from pure content generation and toward representations that better support robot control.
problem_solved: Traditional video generative models are optimized for visual quality and creativity, but this creates a domain mismatch for robotics and embodied AI, where physical realism, action understanding, and compute efficiency are more important.
method: Build a DiT-based video pretraining framework tailored for embodied intelligence.
Replace dense parameterization with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) to improve scaling and computational efficiency.
Pretrain on video data to learn motion-aware, action-relevant representations that transfer better to robot control tasks.
impact: This work offers a scalable path to turn general video models into more useful foundation models for robotics and embodied AI. For practitioners, it suggests a way to improve transfer to downstream control tasks while keeping training more efficient.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline showing standard video generation vs embodied-intelligence-focused pretraining
Architecture diagram of the DiT + MoE framework with expert routing
Comparison chart of dense vs MoE compute/scale tradeoffs
Robot control illustration showing video features transferring to action policy learning
paper_title: Scaling Mixture-of-Experts Video Pretraining for Embodied Intelligence
paper_authors: Shuailei Ma, Jiaqi Liao, Xinyang Wang, Jingjing Wang, Chaoran Feng
